51.title: Rooted Where You Are: A Prayer from Psalm 1 | Evening Meditations
51.desc: A reading of Psalm 1, the picture of a tree planted by streams of water. Tonight you can stop asking why you were put in a dry place and start noticing that the roots can still reach water. The prayer asks God to grow something good in you right where you are. Scripture: Psalm 1:1-3.

52.title: My Refuge and My Strength: A Breath Prayer (Psalm 46:1) | Evening Meditations
52.desc: A short breath prayer from the first line of Psalm 46. Breathe in "You are my refuge," breathe out "You are my strength," and keep going on your own in the quiet. God is not a help that shows up late. He is already in the middle of whatever you are facing tonight. Scripture: Psalm 46:1.

53.title: His Love Endures: A Gratitude Prayer (Psalm 136:1-3) | Evening Meditations
53.desc: A gratitude prayer built on the line that repeats twenty-six times in Psalm 136: his love endures forever. You will name something that lasted through today, someone who stayed, and the love that does not end. It is a good prayer for anyone who has learned how rare lasting things can be. Scripture: Psalm 136:1-3.

54.title: Why Do You Stand Far Off? A Lament Prayer (Psalm 10:1) | Evening Meditations
54.desc: A lament for the nights when God feels far away. Psalm 10 asks the question out loud, and tonight you can ask it too. You will tell God where he seems distant, what you need him to see, and ask him to come close. If you cannot say "You see me" yet, "I want to believe you do" is an honest prayer. Scripture: Psalm 10:1.

55.title: When You Are on Your Bed, Be Silent: A Prayer of Stillness (Psalm 4:4) | Evening Meditations
55.desc: A stillness prayer for bedtime. Psalm 4 says that when you are on your bed, you should search your heart and be silent, because the quiet is when you finally hear yourself. After a short reading we sit in a few quiet minutes with two words to come back to: "be silent" and "I'm here." Scripture: Psalm 4:4.

56.title: Answer Me When I'm in Trouble: A Blessing for the Week (Psalm 20:1-4) | Evening Meditations
56.desc: A blessing for the week ahead from Psalm 20, a prayer that God would answer you in distress, protect you, and send help. You will finish by thinking of someone who may need help this week and asking God to send it, maybe through you. Scripture: Psalm 20:1-4.

57.title: Examine My Heart and Mind: An Evening Examen (Psalm 26:2) | Evening Meditations
57.desc: An examen built on a brave prayer: Lord, examine my heart and my mind. You will look at what you actually thought about today, what it says about what you care about and fear, and what to set down. It ends with one true and good thing to keep your mind on tomorrow. Scripture: Psalm 26:2.

58.title: Mindful of You: A Prayer from Psalm 8 | Evening Meditations
58.desc: A reading of Psalm 8 under a wide night sky. The God who set every star in place is mindful of you, and he has crowned you with glory and honor, no matter what anyone else has called you. The prayer is a slow reminder of who you are tonight. Scripture: Psalm 8:3-5.

59.title: Good News of Great Joy: A Christmas Eve Breath Prayer (Luke 2:10-11) | Evening Meditations
59.desc: A Christmas Eve breath prayer from the words the angel spoke to shepherds on a night shift. Breathe in "Do not be afraid," breathe out "Good news of great joy," and keep going on your own in the quiet. If this is a hard night to be apart from the people you love, this prayer is for you too. Scripture: Luke 2:10-11.

60.title: An Indescribable Gift: A Christmas Day Gratitude Prayer (2 Corinthians 9:15) | Evening Meditations
60.desc: A gratitude prayer for Christmas Day. Paul ran out of words and called Jesus an indescribable gift. You will say thank you for that gift, for something you were given this year, and for something you could give. The prayer also remembers everyone who is missing someone today. Scripture: 2 Corinthians 9:15.

61.title: Every Sigh Is Heard: A Lament Prayer (Psalm 38:9, 15) | Evening Meditations
61.desc: A lament for people who are worn out from carrying it all alone. Psalm 38 says your sighing is not hidden from God, so tonight you let it out. You will name what you long for, what you are tired of carrying, and end with the writer's words: Lord, I wait for you. Scripture: Psalm 38:9 and Psalm 38:15.

62.title: Not Shaken: A Quiet Prayer of Stillness (Psalm 16:8-9) | Evening Meditations
62.desc: A stillness prayer from Psalm 16, written by someone who kept his eyes on one thing so that nothing else could shake him. After a short reading, we sit in a few quiet minutes with two words to come back to: "eyes on You" and "not shaken." Scripture: Psalm 16:8-9.

63.title: Strength and Peace: A Blessing for the Week (Psalm 29:11) | Evening Meditations
63.desc: A short blessing for the week ahead from Psalm 29. God gives strength to his people and blesses them with peace, two things you cannot make for yourself. You will finish by thinking of one person who needs strength or peace this week. Scripture: Psalm 29:11.

64.title: Turn My Steps: An Evening Examen (Psalm 119:59-60) | Evening Meditations
64.desc: An examen for looking at the road you walked today. You will ask which way you were headed, where you took a good step, and where you went the wrong way, without shame. Then you pick one small step to take tomorrow. Scripture: Psalm 119:59-60.

65.title: You Are My Portion: A Prayer from Psalm 16 | Evening Meditations
65.desc: A reading of Psalm 16:5-6 about the portion God gives. The writer talks about boundary lines and calls them pleasant, because his real portion is God himself. Tonight you can choose where to look for your portion, whatever walls are around you. Scripture: Psalm 16:5-6.

66.title: A New Thing: A New Year's Eve Breath Prayer (Isaiah 43:19) | Evening Meditations
66.desc: A breath prayer for the last night of the year. God says he is doing a new thing, making a way in the wilderness and streams in the wasteland, even before we can see it. Breathe in "You are doing a new thing," breathe out "Help me see it," and let the year go. Scripture: Isaiah 43:19.

67.title: Crown the Year: A New Year's Day Gratitude Prayer (Psalm 65:11) | Evening Meditations
67.desc: A gratitude prayer for the first day of the year. Psalm 65 says God crowns the year with his bounty, so tonight you look back and say thank you. You will name something good from last year, something that got you through, and something you are hoping for this year. Scripture: Psalm 65:11.

68.title: Wake Up, Lord: A Lament Prayer (Psalm 44:23-26) | Evening Meditations
68.desc: A lament for when God seems to be asleep. Psalm 44 says "Awake, Lord!" out loud, and tonight you can too. You will tell God where it feels like he is not moving, what you are going through, ask him to rise up and help, and hold on to his unfailing love. Scripture: Psalm 44:23-26.

69.title: One Thing: A Quiet Prayer of Stillness (Psalm 27:4) | Evening Meditations
69.desc: A stillness prayer built on Psalm 27:4, where the writer asks for one thing only: to be near God and gaze on his beauty. After a short reading, we sit in a few quiet minutes with two words to come back to: "one thing" and "your presence." Scripture: Psalm 27:4.

70.title: The Lord Remembers Us: A Blessing for the Week (Psalm 115:12-15) | Evening Meditations
70.desc: A blessing for the week ahead from Psalm 115. The Lord remembers us and will bless us, small and great alike, and that includes the people you love. You will finish by thinking of someone near or far and asking God to bless them this week. Scripture: Psalm 115:12-15.

71.title: A Guard Over My Mouth: An Evening Examen (Psalm 141:3-4) | Evening Meditations
71.desc: An examen about your words. You will look at what you said today that built someone up, what tore someone down, and what was underneath it. Then you choose one kind thing to say to one person tomorrow. Scripture: Psalm 141:3-4.

72.title: The Lord Is My Rock: A Prayer from Psalm 18 | Evening Meditations
72.desc: A reading of Psalm 18:1-6, where the writer names God his rock, fortress, shield, and stronghold, then cries out from the tangle and is heard. A slow prayer for a night when you need something solid to stand on. Scripture: Psalm 18:1-6.

73.title: Perfect Peace: A Breath Prayer from Isaiah 26:3 | Evening Meditations
73.desc: A breath prayer from Isaiah 26:3. Breathe in "Perfect peace," breathe out "I trust You," and keep going on your own in the quiet. When your mind wanders, you just come back to the words. Scripture: Isaiah 26:3.

74.title: With All My Heart: A Gratitude Prayer from Psalm 9 | Evening Meditations
74.desc: A gratitude prayer from Psalm 9:1-2. You will name one wonderful thing God did today, one thing you are glad about, and one person you could tell about his goodness. Scripture: Psalm 9:1-2.

75.title: Oh, That I Had Wings: A Lament from Psalm 55 | Evening Meditations
75.desc: A lament from Psalm 55:1-8 for a night when you want to run away from your thoughts, your fears, or this place. The writer says it out loud to God, and so can you. There is no pressure to fix anything. Scripture: Psalm 55:1-8.

76.title: Our Help and Our Shield: A Stillness Prayer from Psalm 33:20 | Evening Meditations
76.desc: A stillness prayer built on Psalm 33:20. After a short reading, we sit in a few quiet minutes with two words to come back to: "help" and "shield." Scripture: Psalm 33:20.
